# tests/fixtures — Golden Vectors for Cross-Reference Validation NeuralAmpModelerCore ↔ NAM-rs

## Source of Truth

All golden vectors in this directory are generated by **NeuralAmpModelerCore** (Steven Atkinson) — the canonical implementation that trains and generates `.nam` models.

## Files in this directory

| Golden File                   | `.nam` Model          | Origin  | Topology                        |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------- |
| `golden_wavenet_standard.bin` | `BossWN-standard.nam` | NAM-rs  | CH=16, K=3, HEAD=8, 20 layers   |
| `golden_wavenet_feather.bin`  | `BossWN-feather.nam`  | NAM-rs  | CH=8, K=3, HEAD=4, 20 layers    |
| `golden_wavenet_nano.bin`     | `BossWN-nano.nam`     | NAM-rs  | CH=4, K=3, HEAD=2, 20 layers    |
| `golden_lstm_1x16.bin`        | `BossLSTM-1x16.nam`   | NAM-rs  | 1 layer, H=16                   |
| `golden_lstm_2x8.bin`         | `BossLSTM-2x8.nam`    | NAM-rs  | 2 layers, H=8                   |
| `golden_namcore_lstm_1x3.bin` | `lstm.nam`            | NAMCore | 1 layer, H=3, 70 weights        |
| `golden_namcore_wn_micro.bin` | `wavenet.nam`         | NAMCore | CH=3/2, K=3, HEAD=2/1, 3 layers |

The 2 NAMCore models (`lstm.nam` and `wavenet.nam`) are from the `example_models/` directory of NeuralAmpModelerCore — the same ones used in the official tests (`test_get_dsp.cpp`, `test_slimmable_wavenet.cpp`). They exercise topologies **below any static profile** of NAM-rs, forcing dynamic dispatch/fallback paths.

## Binary format (.golden.bin)

```text
[u32 num_samples LE]
[f32×N input samples LE]       — stress signal (2048 samples @ 48 kHz)
[f32×N expected output LE]     — output from NeuralAmpModelerCore (render tool)
```

## Stress Signal (2048 samples @ 48 kHz ≈ 42.7 ms)

Replaces the 440 Hz sine wave with a deterministic multi-component signal:

| Behavior to test                         | Signal component                     |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Frequency response (low → high)          | Chirp sweep 220 Hz → 3520 Hz         |
| Harmonic intermodulation (real guitar)   | Low-E harmonics (82/165/330/659 Hz)  |
| Transient response (note attack)         | Isolated impulse (+0.9) at 25%       |
| Amplitude dynamics                       | Attack–sustain–release envelope      |
| Near-silence / denormals behavior        | Fade-to-silence (release tail)       |

## Precision Metrics (5 metrics, single-pass fusion)

Each golden test reports **5 metrics** computed in a single pass over the buffer:

| Metric      | Formula                           | What it detects                            |
| ----------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| **MSE**     | `Σ(rᵢ - tᵢ)² / N`                 | Mean error (structural regressions)        |
| **MAE**     | `max                              | rᵢ - tᵢ                                    |
| **SNR**     | `10 · log₁₀(Σrᵢ² / Σ(rᵢ-tᵢ)²)`    | Signal-to-noise ratio (DSP interpretation) |
| **PSNR**    | `10 · log₁₀(peak² / MSE)`         | SNR normalized by peak                     |
| **Bits eq.** | `-0.5 · log₂(MSE / signal_power)` | Precision — how many correct float32 bits  |

## Parity Thresholds

| Model            | MSE threshold | SNR threshold |
| ---------------- |:-------------:|:-------------:|
| LSTM 1×16        | < 3e-3        | ≥ 15 dB       |
| LSTM 2×8         | < 1e-3        | ≥ 18 dB       |
| NAMCore LSTM 1×3 | < 1e-3        | ≥ 22 dB       |
| WaveNet Nano     | < 5e-2        | ≥ 9 dB        |
| WaveNet Feather  | < 5e-2        | ≥ 9 dB        |
| WaveNet Standard | < 5e-2        | ≥ 9 dB        |
| NAMCore WN Micro | < 5e-2        | ≥ 9 dB        |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The thresholds are empirically calibrated. NAMCore (native `std::tanh`) may show higher SNR than Boss models (FastMath Padé). The divergence is exclusively dominated by the `tanh`/`sigmoid` implementation — see ADR-001 in `docs/architecture.md §2`.

## To regenerate

```bash
./tests/fixtures/golden_gen_build.sh
```

Prerequisites: `cmake`, `g++` (or `clang++`, C++20), `python3`, `git`.

These files are committed to the repository so that the Rust golden vector tests can run without needing to recompile C++. If the golden vectors do not exist, the tests gracefully skip.

## Two Layers of Validation

### Layer 1 — Pre-committed goldens (fast, `cargo test`)

Tests in `tests/nam_infer_test.rs` load the `.golden.bin` files and compare against Rust inference. Runs on every `cargo test` without C++.

### Layer 2 — Live cross-validation (slow, `utils/tests-long.sh`)

`#[ignore]` tests in `tests/cpp_parity.rs` compile the `render` tool from NeuralAmpModelerCore on-demand and compare C++ vs Rust live. Detects drift if NAMCore is updated and the pre-committed goldens become stale.

## Technical Decision: Cross-Reference is NOT Bit-Identical (ADR-002)

> **Decision:** The golden vectors validate *functional* parity (MSE + SNR + PSNR + bits within calibrated thresholds) against NeuralAmpModelerCore C++, **not** *bit-for-bit* parity.
>
> **Consequence:** NAM-rs produces audio perceptually equivalent to C++, but with measurable numerical differences (SNR 9–25 dB depending on the model). These differences are inaudible in any 16-bit or higher audio pipeline.
>
> **Exclusive source of divergence:** `tanh` and `sigmoid` implementations — see ADR-001 in `docs/architecture.md §2`.
>
> **Proof:** SNR degradation is proportional to model depth:
>
> - LSTM 1×16 (1 layer): SNR ~25 dB
> - WaveNet Standard (20 layers): SNR ~10 dB
>
> If there were a structural error, SNR would not degrade linearly with depth.
